newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains, still up on foreign buys.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains, still up on foreign buys.

text.p: Mexican stocks shied away from earlier record levels in brisk midday trade Friday, but were still ahead on a heavy inflow of foreign capital, dealers said.
"I feel there was some light profit-taking when the Dow went off the boil because prices are very high, but there is still demand and a lot of foreign money in the bourse," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 25.30 points, or 0.60 percent, at 4,265.32. The IPC had earlier set an intraday record of 4,291.11 points.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 78.26 points at 7789.73, but down from a historic level of 7,837.23 reached earlier.
The level of foreign participation in the bourse was evident from high volume of 102.2 million shares traded.

"Foreigners are pouring most of their money into financials, the market seems to believe a past-due loans restructuring plan is in the wings," the trader added. "Apart from that, the market is very selective."
The Bancomer financial group, one of Mexico's biggest, was up 28 centavos to 3.68 pesos.
Bancomer's A shares were meanwhile up six centavos to 1.94 pesos. The two share series together accounted for more than one-quarter of all shares traded.
The BBV-Probursa financial group was meanwhile up 8 centavos to 2.09 pesos at heavy trade.

Financial groups also headed the percentage gainers' list .PG.MX, with the Abaco group in first place with a gain of 8 centavos to 82 centavos. Banacci L shares followed Abaco, up 1.54 pesos to 18.40 pesos.
Dealers said profit-taking was most evident in market heavyweight Telmex, off 4 centavos to 18.96 pesos.
The telecom's ADRs were meanwhile down 3/8 to 47-5/8.
On the broad market, of 113 stocks traded, gainers outpaced sliders by 62 to 32.
